source.candidate_subject: perf: select Decode gate-up dead-up staging
source.measurement_relationship: The frozen binary was built from the uncommitted source/test bytes subsequently committed without modification as candidate_commit.

environment.comparison_scope: three independent clean processes of one frozen exact-shape candidate binary on the named device
environment.claim_boundary: This same-binary microbenchmark selects a runner-contract candidate. It is not an achieved end-to-end latency, throughput, thermal, power, or cross-device result.

candidate.phase: exact M1 Decode post-attention residual add, centered RMSNorm, NVFP4 gate/up, and SiLU
candidate.dtype: BF16 residual/norm inputs and outputs; NVFP4 E2M1 packed weights with FP8 E4M3FN block scales
candidate.mechanism: Keep the independently BF16-rounded gate and up projection intermediates in two CTA-local 576-entry BF16 shared arrays. After both projection phases, publish only the final BF16-RNE SiLU(gate)*up vector; the runner-dead up_output buffer remains untouched.
candidate.row_mapping: Each warp writes four CTA-local rows per 2,048-row global stride. Logical blocks 0 through 15 use nine 64-row CTA strides with maximum local index 575; blocks 16 through 31 use eight strides with maximum local index 511. A full-CTA barrier precedes the balanced 512-thread SiLU epilogue.
candidate.arithmetic_contract: Residual add, centered RMSNorm, projection FFMA and warp-reduction order, independent gate/up BF16-RNE boundaries, SiLU arithmetic, final BF16-RNE, and global row mapping match production for every published output.

global_intermediate_traffic_removed.formula: 17408 rows * 2 bytes * two tensors * one write plus one read
global_intermediate_traffic_removed.measurement_scope: logical eliminated global-memory instructions and bytes, not measured DRAM transactions

candidate.scope_boundary: The selected launcher, query, and kernel remain test-only. The existing public low-level and high-level gate/up APIs still promise an independently rounded up_output and must not be changed to this behavior. Production integration requires a new explicit Decode-runner-only dead-up contract.

cuda_graph_capture_contract.limitation: This selection capture used aligned sentinel pointers to prove single-node topology and distinct function identity; real-buffer Graph instantiate/replay remains a production-integration gate.

invalid_calls.production_integration_requirement: The runner-only production API must inherit the complete shared validator matrix, including all null, nonfinite scalar, alignment, shape, and alias cases.

sass.normalization: cuobjdump Function section; every ordered 64-bit encoding/control word emitted as one lowercase 0x-prefixed line before SHA-256

performance_protocol.comparison: within each clean process, production exact 32x512 double-publication kernel versus test-only exact 32x512 CTA-local dead-up candidate in one frozen binary, stream, and fixture
performance_protocol.cross_process_reporting_statistic: median of the three within-process paired-round medians

excluded_measurement.exclusion_reason: An unrelated historical 64x256-versus-32x512 CTA-coarsen comparator suffered a single 0.966306x actual-checkpoint round after a 0.677115-ms production pass, so the whole suite failed its already-promoted comparator assertion.
excluded_measurement.dead_up_candidate_behavior: The dead-up candidate itself passed all ten actual/stress rounds in this excluded process, with paired medians 1.01244x and 1.01293x. It is retained for transparency but contributes no clean-process statistic.

decision.reason: Three independent clean same-binary processes clear the actual and stress median gates, all 30 clean paired rounds improve, published residual/final outputs are bitwise exact for finite and signed Inf/NaN fixtures, the dead up workspace remains untouched, and resource, Graph-capture, invalid-call, production-SASS-identity, and default-test gates pass.
next_required_work: add an explicit internal runner-only dead-up API while preserving the generic double-output API and all fallbacks
prove with runner call-chain tests that up_workspace is dead until the down projection overwrites it
run real-buffer CUDA Graph instantiate/replay and the complete invalid-input matrix on the production API
run Release/default/CTest, pinned C1/C8/C16/C32 full-model oracles, and exact trace equivalence
run fixed-frequency P19/C32/max26 B1-C1-C2-B2 end-to-end Decode measurement
capture a fresh production Decode Nsys trace before changing the formal anchor
decision.promotion_gate: Only final production-runner integration plus model-oracle, end-to-end, and profile evidence may change the formal 109.056-ms/token and 9.169600939-token/s anchor.

limitations: The selected launcher and kernel are test-only; no production route or public ABI changed.
The existing public APIs require an independently rounded up_output. Only an explicit runner-private contract may elide that publication.
The fixed clock configuration was retained during the clean processes, but no standalone before/after clock, thermal, power, or energy log is archived with this selection.

Actual-checkpoint microbenchmark payloads come from pinned layer 0; same-bank stress and exact arithmetic contracts broaden data coverage, but only the full-model runner validation covers all 64 layers.
The Graph gate proves capture topology with aligned sentinel pointers; real-buffer instantiate/replay remains required during production integration.
The representative nine-case invalid-call probe relies on the shared complete validator; the production runner-only API must re-run the complete null/scalar/alignment/shape/alias matrix.

One whole-suite process was excluded transparently because an unrelated historical comparator had a single large outlier; its dead-up measurements passed but are not used in the clean-process statistic.
No production runner, full-model oracle, end-to-end Decode benchmark, Nsys, or NCU measurement is attached to this selection.
The 0.396352-ms/token planning value and 0.367232-to-0.409216-ms/token range are linear 64-layer arithmetic projections, not achieved latency reductions.
The formal performance anchor remains 109.056 ms/token and 9.169600939 token/s until final production integration and end-to-end validation pass.
The result does not measure Prefill, multi-request serving, energy, or behavior on another device or clock configuration.
